# AGENTS

This repository contains two runtime surfaces:

- `apps/web/` for the Next.js web app (UI + API routes).
- `services/chat/` for the FastAPI chat service.

Use this file as the default runbook for coding agents.

## Source of truth

`AGENTS.md` is the canonical format for agent instructions. The root file defines
repository-wide policy; a nested `AGENTS.md` adds authoritative instructions for
its subtree. Apply both, from the root down to the file closest to the work.

Assistant-specific context files are pointers only. They contain no independent
instructions:

| Assistant | Pointer file | Points at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` (per scope) | sibling `AGENTS.md` |
| Gemini CLI | `GEMINI.md` (per scope) | sibling `AGENTS.md` |
| GitHub Copilot | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | root `AGENTS.md` |

Scopes with their own runbook:

- `AGENTS.md` (repo-wide)
- `apps/web/AGENTS.md`
- `services/chat/AGENTS.md`
- `tests/scripts/AGENTS.md`

Never add instructions to a pointer file. That includes memories captured by pressing
`#` in Claude Code, which append to the nearest `CLAUDE.md` — move that text into the
matching `AGENTS.md` instead.

`make agent-docs-check` (part of `make docs-check`, and gated in CI) fails when a
pointer drifts and prints the added lines. To restore the pointers locally after
moving the content across:

```bash
make agent-docs-check FIX=1
```

## Code Review Rules

- Treat changes at system seams as one contract. When a change touches the web/chat
  payload, Prisma schema and handwritten SQL, dependency manifests and constraints,
  or container inputs and runtime files, inspect and validate both sides.
- Require guards to measure effective behavior, not a nearby declaration. Reject
  vacuous loops, mislabeled samples, or configuration checks that never exercise the
  rendered pixels, served bytes, accessibility tree, resolved files, or tool output
  named by the assertion.
- For runtime and container changes, verify the built artifact and real integration
  path. Unit tests cannot prove that a file was copied into an image, a service starts
  with its deployed configuration, or the web/chat/database path works together.

## Development workflow

Follow these steps in order for every change.

1. **Inspect before changing anything.** Inspect the repository, current Git
   state, and all applicable instruction files before making changes. Preserve
   unrelated staged, unstaged, and untracked work.

2. **Create a branch first.** Create a dedicated feature, fix, refactor, chore,
   test, or documentation branch before making code changes. Never commit
   directly to `main`, and create the branch from the latest appropriate
   `main` state.

3. **Choose a thin vertical slice.** Before implementing a tracked issue or
   feature, define the smallest end-to-end slice that can be reviewed, tested,
   shipped, and merged independently. Prefer one coherent user-visible or
   operational outcome over a broad horizontal layer. If the next issue is too
   large for one pull request, split it into ordered slices and complete only
   the current slice. Keep pull requests small enough for thorough review,
   reliable verification, and quick rollback.

4. **Use test-driven development when behavior or structure is testable.**
   - Add or update a focused test before implementation.
   - Run it and confirm it fails for the expected reason.
   - Implement the smallest appropriate change.
   - Run focused tests while iterating.
   - Refactor only while the relevant tests remain green.

   **A guard added for behavior that already works has no red phase**, so the
   confirm-it-fails bullet never reaches it. Write down which mistake each
   assertion catches, and which ones nothing catches, then demonstrate it:
   break an input on purpose and watch that assertion fail on it. Coverage
   argued rather than demonstrated is the defect the guard was added to
   prevent, one level up.

   **Measure what was produced, not what was asked for.** A guard that reads a
   declaration is measuring the request, and the two come apart constantly: a
   colour Tailwind serialises as `lab()` reads as a different colour through a
   regex for numbers; `ring-0` leaves its colour in the computed box-shadow
   with no geometry to paint it; a zero-width border still reports a border
   colour; a blurred shadow reports its source colour while every pixel it
   paints is composited toward the background; `outlineWidth` reports the
   user-agent default of `3px` for an outline whose style is `none`. Every one
   of those passed a check that looked right and was measuring something
   adjacent to the claim. Read the rendered pixels, the served bytes, the
   accessibility tree — whatever the asserted thing actually is.

   The same trap catches fixtures and samples. Assert that a sample is what its
   name says — for example, a brightness band, an overlap, or a count that only
   the intended case produces. Fixture-isolation rules for the root guard suite
   live in `tests/scripts/AGENTS.md`.

   **Run the focused test here, and only the focused test.** This step needs
   the one spec or module under change, its red phase, and the mutations that
   demonstrate what each assertion catches. The `verifier` will not do those:
   it is instructed not to modify the repository, so breaking an input on
   purpose is not available to it. Fast whole-suite runners are fine too where
   they are genuinely fast — `make test-web` is a few seconds.

   The one spec may itself be a journey, and then it needs a composed stack:
   `make e2e-smoke KEEP_STACK=1` builds one and leaves it up, and steps 6 and 7
   will want that same one. No make target runs a single spec, so running just
   the one is `npx playwright test <file>` from `apps/web`.

   What does not belong here is the whole journey suite. Running it costs
   minutes per iteration, and the trigger for handing over is "I believe this
   is done", not "I want to know whether it works".

5. **Inspect the complete diff.** Review the branch diff plus all staged,
   unstaged, and untracked files. Remove accidental or unrelated changes while
   preserving work that belongs to the user. A real problem found here is filed
   as an issue before the change is removed — see *Unrelated findings become
   issues* below.

6. **Run `ui-review` before verification.** After the main agent completes an
   implementation pass, invoke the `ui-review` sub-agent. The `ui-review`
   sub-agent must act as an expert in website design, usability,
   responsiveness, and accessibility. Address every actionable finding before
   running the `verifier`. For UI-affecting changes, exercise the changed
   journey in the rendered application at representative phone, tablet, and
   desktop viewports; inspect interaction, loading, empty, error, focus,
   keyboard, contrast, and responsive states as applicable; and capture
   screenshots or equivalent visual evidence.

   A viewport is a width in CSS pixels, which says nothing about how many
   device pixels fill it. Where the change affects what the browser requests —
   anything carrying a `srcset`, or a source whose dimensions changed —
   exercise it at **2x as well as 1x**. Density is a property of the browser
   context (`deviceScaleFactor: 2`), not a width, so it needs a second pass
   rather than another viewport. A 2x screen asks for twice the CSS width, and
   the optimiser never upscales past the source, so a source that satisfies 1x
   can fall short at 2x while every 1x measurement stays clean. The 600px
   re-encode first tried in #152 came out at −0.9 to −2.2 dB PSNR at 1x and
   −4.4 to −6.6 dB at 2x: a difference at 1x small enough to accept, and one at
   2x that was plainly visible.

   A change is UI-affecting when it moves a rendering dependency, too —
   `tailwindcss`, `next`, `react`, `postcss`, or a UI library in
   `apps/web/package.json`. That diff touches no component and can still change
   every rendered pixel; a Tailwind major shipped here with every check green.

   For changes with no UI impact, explicitly record that rendered UI review is
   not applicable. If a finding is not applicable, record the concrete reason
   rather than silently ignoring it.

   `ui-review` may start and stop a stack of its own. If one is already up —
   from step 4, or from an earlier pass through steps 6 and 7 when step 8 sends
   you back here — give it the `E2E_BASE_URL` and the ports if they are not the
   defaults, say the stack is not to be torn down, and say it is not
   `ui-review`'s. Naming it without addressing it is not a handover: remapped
   ports are normal here, and a reviewer that cannot reach the stack starts its
   own or renders nothing. Otherwise step 7's handover below promises a stack
   that stopped existing here.

7. **Run `verifier` before code review.** Invoke the `verifier` sub-agent to run
   the builds, static checks, tests, and journey coverage appropriate for the
   change. The verifier must report failures, flakes, missing coverage, and
   environment issues. Fix or explicitly resolve every actionable finding
   before starting code review. If a verifier finding requires a code change,
   rerun the verifier after addressing it.

   **The whole battery belongs here** — the merge-gate command, the production
   build, the root guard suite, and the full journey run. Do not pre-run those
   and hand over a summary: it doubles the wall-clock, and a summary is not
   what the next step needs.

   **Hand over the stack rather than leaving one to be found.** Where journeys
   need a composed stack, step 4 has usually built one, and step 6 may have
   built its own — `ui-review` is allowed to, and that one is then its to tear
   down and may be on ports it chose. Give the `E2E_BASE_URL`, say the stack is
   yours, and say `KEEP_STACK=1`: without that flag `make e2e-smoke` deletes
   the containers and their volumes on exit. What the handover buys is not the
   rebuild, which happens either way, but that the verifier knows a stack
   exists, knows where it is, and knows not to destroy it. Tear it down after
   the last step that needs it, not after this one.

   Say the ports if they are not the defaults. `make test-e2e` follows
   `E2E_BASE_URL` anywhere; `make e2e-smoke` probes `127.0.0.1:3100` and
   `:8100` literally and cannot be aimed elsewhere, so it and a remapped stack
   do not mix. One of the ways they fail is a green smoke run against an
   unrelated project's containers, which is worse than a failure because
   nothing looks wrong. Exactly which way you get depends on which compose
   files resolve and which ports are already held, and is not worth predicting
   here. Free the default ports before step 7, or hand over nothing and say
   why.

8. **Run `code-review` before every commit.** Invoke the `code-review`
   sub-agent against the current branch diff and every staged, unstaged, and
   untracked file. The reviewer must act as an expert in the languages and
   frameworks used by this application. Address every actionable finding
   before committing. If review findings cause changes, rerun the appropriate
   tests and the `verifier`, then obtain a fresh `code-review` approval for the
   changed state.

   That loop has no natural end, so ask for one: **have the reviewer say which
   findings are defects and which are refinements.** The loop ends on a round
   returning no defects, however many refinements come with it. Apply those,
   rerun the focused tests and the `verifier`, and record what was applied — a
   refinement-only change does not earn a fresh review round, here or at
   step 10.

   **A fix made in this loop can invalidate step 6 as well.** If it alters what
   a page renders, rerun `ui-review` before the verifier and carry its verdict
   forward; the screenshots from step 6 otherwise describe a state that no
   longer exists. If it does not, record that the fix was not UI-affecting and
   go straight to the verifier. Only defects reopen step 6, on the same
   reasoning that ends this loop — a refinement applied to a rendered surface
   does not.

9. **Commit after approval.** Commit only after verification and code review
   are complete. Use Conventional Commits:

   ```text
   <type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>
   ```

   Keep the subject at 72 characters or fewer, describe why in the body when
   useful, and do not combine unrelated work.

10. **Create pull requests from the reviewed state.**
    - Confirm that local verification remains valid.
    - Rerun `code-review` only if the reviewed state changed after the
      pre-commit review.
    - A changed state includes code, tests, documentation, generated files,
      conflict resolution, or any other staged, unstaged, or untracked content.
    - Except refinements the reviewer classified as such and step 8 cleared:
      applying those does not re-arm this, or the loop step 8 just ended
      reopens here.
    - Do not repeat code review when the already-reviewed diff and worktree
      remain unchanged.
    - Updating the branch from `main` — rebase, merge, or conflict resolution —
      invalidates **verification** as well as review. The builds, merge gates,
      smoke, and journeys were measured against a tree that no longer exists,
      so rerun step 7's applicable commands against the updated one rather than
      rerunning `code-review` alone.
    - Tear down any stack steps 4, 6, or 7 left running, once step 8's loop has
      closed and no further `verifier` run is coming: `make down`, or
      `docker compose down --volumes` to drop the seeded database with it. Step
      7 hands its stack forward under `KEEP_STACK=1`, which disables the only
      teardown the workflow otherwise performs — so without this the containers
      outlive the change and hold ports 3100, 55432, and 8100 against the next
      one.
    - Push and create the pull request only after local verification and any
      required code review are complete.
# AGENTS (Web)

Web app scope for coding agents. This file adds authoritative instructions for
`apps/web/`; apply it together with the repo-root `AGENTS.md`. Put instructions
here, never in `apps/web/CLAUDE.md` or `apps/web/GEMINI.md`.

## Entry points

- Routes: `src/app/`
- UI components: `src/components/`
- Domain and API clients: `src/lib/`
- Route tests: `src/app/**/*.test.tsx` and `src/app/**/*.test.ts`

## Local commands

From repository root:

```bash
make bootstrap
make agent-doctor
make dev-web
make lint
make typecheck
make test-web
npm run bootstrap
npm run doctor
npm run dev:web
npm run ci:web
```

From the web app directory:

```bash
make help
make setup
make dev
make quick-ci
make ci
```

## Chat integration touchpoints

- Web proxy route: `src/app/api/chat/service/route.ts`
- Web chat client: `src/lib/messaging.ts`

When changing a request or response shape, update the chat service and its tests
in `services/chat/` as part of the same change.

## Database access

Prisma 7 removed `url` from the schema's `datasource` block. The connection URL
now lives in two places, both reading `DATABASE_URL`:

- `prisma.config.ts` — used by `prisma migrate` and `prisma db seed`.
- A `PrismaPg` driver adapter passed to every `PrismaClient` constructor
  (`src/lib/prisma.ts` and `prisma/seed.ts`). Constructing `PrismaClient`
  without an adapter fails at runtime.

The production image builds with `NEXT_BUILD_SKIP_DB=1`, so anything Next
prerenders at build time captures the no-database response permanently. Route
handlers that read the database must opt out of static prerendering.

## Code Review Rules

- A route that reads the database must remain dynamic under the production
  `NEXT_BUILD_SKIP_DB=1` build. Flag a change that can bake a build-time empty or
  fallback response into the deployed route instead of evaluating it at request time.
- Treat the web proxy, `src/lib/messaging.ts`, and the FastAPI request/response
  models as one contract. A payload change is incomplete unless both surfaces and
  their contract tests agree, including error and degraded responses.
- For UI changes, review the rendered behavior rather than class names alone.
  Preserve keyboard/focus semantics and responsive states; when `srcset` or source
  dimensions change, require evidence at representative 1x and 2x densities.

## JavaScript, TypeScript, and React conventions

- Prefer functions, plain objects, and ES module boundaries when no instance identity
  or lifecycle is required. Plain objects are mutable; never mutate React state, and
  use a class when an external API or a test double genuinely requires one.
- Avoid `any` and unchecked type assertions at application boundaries. Accept
  `unknown`, validate or narrow it, and keep unavoidable assertions local with a
  reason the compiler cannot establish the type itself.
- Prefer non-mutating collection operations. `sort()` mutates; use `toSorted()` when
  supported or sort a deliberate copy such as `[...items].sort(...)`.
- Keep rendering pure and use functional components and Hooks. Effects synchronize
  with external systems; derive values during render or update them in event handlers
  when no external synchronization is involved. Clean up subscriptions and include
  the dependencies the effect reads.
- Do not assume React Compiler is enabled. Check the current Next configuration before
  relying on compiler memoization, and add `useMemo`, `useCallback`, or `React.memo`
  only when referential identity or measured performance makes it necessary.
- Keep environment access centralized, avoid service URLs in components, and prefer
  focused tests beside changed routes, components, and library modules.
# AGENTS (Chat Service)

FastAPI chat service scope for coding agents. This file adds authoritative
instructions for `services/chat/`; apply it together with the repo-root
`AGENTS.md`. Put instructions here, never in `services/chat/CLAUDE.md` or
`services/chat/GEMINI.md`.

## Entry points

- API app: `services/chat/src/api/main.py`
- Chat logic: `services/chat/src/api/contoso_chat/`
- Evaluators: `services/chat/src/api/evaluators/`
- Tests: `services/chat/tests/unit/`
- Integration coverage: `scripts/e2e_smoke.py`, run by `make e2e-smoke` against a real stack

## Toolchain baseline

- Python `3.11` (matches CI for chat checks)

From repository root:

```bash
mise install
make venv
```

All chat Python runs from the shared repo-root virtualenv at `.venv`. The Make
targets here create it on demand and call `.venv/bin/python` directly, so no
activation step is needed. Do not `pip install` chat dependencies into a system
or mise interpreter.

## Local commands

From repository root:

```bash
make bootstrap
make agent-doctor
make setup-chat
make local-provider-check
make diagnose-chat-local
make dev-chat
make test-chat
npm run bootstrap
npm run doctor
npm run setup:chat
npm run local-provider-check
npm run diagnose:chat:local
npm run dev:chat
npm run ci:chat
```

From service directory:

```bash
make help
make check-python
make setup
make local-provider-check
make diagnose-chat-local
make dev
make deps-check
make lint
make typecheck
make test
make quick-ci
make ci
```

Integration checks run against a real stack from the repository root:

```bash
make e2e-smoke
```

## Environment

Use `services/chat/.env.example` as the baseline template.

Most common local values:

- `LLM_PROVIDER=local`
- `OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434`
- `ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3100`

## Database access

The chat service reads Postgres directly through `asyncpg` in
`services/chat/src/api/db.py`. There is no generated Python ORM client and no
code generation step.

`prisma-client-py` was removed: it pinned Prisma 5.17.0 and required a `url` in
the shared schema's `datasource` block, which Prisma 7 removes. Generating both
a JS and a Python client from `apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma` meant the Python
client dictated which Prisma versions the web app could adopt.

`apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma` remains the source of truth for the data model
and migrations. When it changes, update the SQL in `db.py` to match — the
queries name tables and columns explicitly and nothing verifies them at build
time.

## Code Review Rules

- Treat `apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma` and the handwritten `asyncpg` queries as
  one data contract. Schema changes must update affected SQL and exercise the
  real migration/query path; a successful Python build cannot detect drift.
- Preserve the web/chat API contract across FastAPI models, the web proxy, and
  `apps/web/src/lib/messaging.ts`. Request, success, validation, degraded, and
  error shapes must change together with unit and contract coverage.
- Keep provider choice and credentials behind environment variables. Core chat
  paths must not import optional local-LLM/vector dependencies unless the full
  profile is selected, and dependency versions belong in `constraints.txt`.
# AGENTS (Script Guardrails)

Root script-test scope for coding agents. This file adds authoritative
instructions for `tests/scripts/`; apply it together with the repo-root
`AGENTS.md`. Put instructions here, never in the sibling pointer files.

## Local commands

Run from the repository root:

```bash
make test-scripts
.venv/bin/python -m unittest tests.scripts.<module> -v
```

## Code Review Rules

- Point a guard demonstration at a fixture tree, never the checkout it protects.
  Rebind every imported path constant the assertion dereferences; changing a root
  after derived constants were created does not redirect those constants.
- Prove that the intended assertion catches its named mistake, and separately prove
  the fixture was opened. A vacuity failure on an empty or mistyped path is not
  evidence that the behavioral assertion ran.
- Compare effective sets and outputs from the owning tool where practical. Parsing
  one declaration is insufficient when includes, excludes, defaults, comments, or
  other configuration can change what the compiler, runner, or hook actually uses.

## Fixture isolation

These modules compute path constants at import, so read the module and rebind every
constant the demonstrated assertion reaches:

- `test_image_encoding.py` reaches its files through `IMAGES_DIR`.
- `test_image_references.py` also needs `PUBLIC_DIR`, which `relative_to` depends on,
  and `REPO_ROOT`, which it walks for references.
- `test_page_headings.py` reads `REPO_ROOT` directly for component-supplied headings,
  so rebinding `APP_DIR` alone leaves that assertion pointed at the checkout.
- `test_published_ports.py` needs both `REPO_ROOT`, which `read()` resolves every
  coupled file through, and `COMPOSE`, which the port parser opens directly.
  Rebinding one leaves half the comparison pointed at the checkout, and the halves
  agreeing is the whole assertion.
- `test_agent_doctor.py` loads `scripts/agent_doctor.py` as a module, so the
  constants to rebind are that module's `COMPOSE_FILE`, `ROOT_ENV` and `CHAT_ENV` —
  not this file's `REPO_ROOT`, which only locates the script to load. Its
  `stale_port_keys` tests take their inputs as arguments and reach no path at all,
  which is the reason they are shaped that way.

Confirm the run opened the fixture with a failure that names a fixture path or a
vacuity guard whose count matches what the fixture contains. The count is the
evidence: a vacuity guard also fires when a fixture path is mistyped, while every
assertion inside the resulting empty loop passes.

issues.title: Working agreement for the autonomous maintenance loop
issues.body:
Durable context for whoever — or whatever — picks this up next. Kept as an issue rather than in an agent's local memory so it survives a cleared context and is visible to everyone.

## How this repository is being worked

Changes go through the [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md) workflow end to end: branch, implement, ui-review, verifier, code-review, PR. PRs merge when CI is green. Findings become issues. The loop continues to the next item without pausing for step-by-step approval.

The point is that it runs unattended, so stopping to confirm each step defeats it.

## What still gets surfaced rather than decided silently

Proceeding by default does not mean deciding everything. Three categories get a recommendation and a question:

1. **Changes to what users see** — image quality, layout tradeoffs. #96 is the live example: re-encoding to WebP is well-measured, but q82/600px is a judgment about acceptable fidelity, not a fact.
2. **Changes to other contributors' behavior** — #147 committed tool config that runs hooks on anyone's machine who clones. That deserved saying out loud, not just doing.
3. **Rewrites of shared history** — never silently. See the note below on why this keeps coming up.

The rest of the work does not wait on those answers. Finish everything that does not depend on the decision first, then ask.

## Two things that have repeatedly caught people out

**Checks that run without asserting on what they produced.** This is the repo's signature defect, found three separate times: the E2E smoke passed against a chat service returning `fallback: true`; the seed ran green on every PR while writing credentials that could never authenticate (#141); a category page referenced an image that had never existed (#137). A green check is not evidence unless something inspects its output.

**Verifying in a richer environment than the real one.** Also recurring: a populated local venv vs CI's bare one; jsdom vs a real browser; three sampled viewports vs the breakpoint boundaries where the defects actually live; `node_modules` vs the standalone image; a local stack reading `.env` vs CI with none. If a check passes locally, confirm it runs in the environment that matters.

**Deleting files does not shrink `git clone`.** The blobs stay reachable from history. #146 removed 68.6 MB from the working tree and the web image; `size-pack` did not move. Worth remembering before promising a clone-size win — see the measurement in #66.

## Running the stack locally

Environments differ per machine (port collisions, whether Ollama is installed for `LLM_PROVIDER=local`). `make e2e-smoke` may need a compose override for ports and provider. Resolve collisions with an override file using `ports: !override` — a plain `ports:` list appends rather than replaces — and never by stopping containers you did not start.

## Current state

`main` is clean. #145, #146 and #147 are merged. Open: #96 (WebP re-encode, the next substantive item), #66 (image weight, parent of #96), #118 (import-declaration guardrail), #129 (chat panel below `sm`, needs a design decision), #69 and #90 (blocked upstream).

issues.title: Every page fetches /api/categories on load, for a drawer most visitors never open
issues.body:
Found by `code-review` during #306.

## Measured

`apps/web/src/components/sidebar-wrapper.tsx:17-31`:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  async function fetchCategories() {
    ...
    const response = await fetch("/api/categories");
    ...
  }
  fetchCategories();
}, []);
```

An empty dependency array on a mount effect, in a component `Header` renders unconditionally. So the request fires on every page load of every route that has a header — six of them — regardless of whether the visitor ever opens the drawer. The result is held in component state, so it is not shared between navigations either: a client-side route change remounts the header and fetches again.

The only consumer is the drawer's Shop section.

## Why it is worth recording

The endpoint reads the database. `services/chat` and the web app share that database, and `/api/categories` is on the request path of every page view rather than of a feature — so the load it generates is proportional to traffic rather than to use of the menu.

It also interacts with two issues already open on this component:

- **#308** — the failure path renders a heading with an empty list and no error. Fetching eagerly means that failure is reached on every page load rather than only when someone opens the drawer, which is the difference between a silent empty menu and a silent empty menu that has already cost a database round trip.
- **#312 / general boundary typing** — the same effect's `useState([])` infers `never[]`, noted on #308.

## Options

1. **Fetch on first open.** The drawer already knows when it opens; moving the fetch there costs one request only when the menu is used, at the price of a moment's latency the first time. That latency is the argument for the current design, and it is worth stating rather than assuming it away.
2. **Hoist it to a server component or the layout**, so it is fetched once per document rather than once per header mount, and can be prerendered with the page.
3. **Cache it** — `/api/categories` output changes rarely, so a shared client cache or an HTTP cache header would cut the repeat cost without moving the call.

## Not established

How expensive the endpoint actually is, and whether it is already cached at the HTTP layer. Neither was measured — this is a structural observation from reading the effect, and the fix should be chosen against a number rather than against the shape of the code.

issues.title: Contact fields have empty autocomplete, and /contact renders two <main> elements
issues.body:
Two small pre-existing defects on the same page, found by `ui-review` during #196 and unrelated to it.

## 1. No `autocomplete` on the contact fields

`apps/web/src/components/contact-form.tsx` — the name and email inputs carry an empty `autocomplete`. WCAG 2.2 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (Level AA) asks for the purpose to be programmatically identifiable on fields collecting information about the user, and `name` and `email` are both on the list of purposes it names.

The practical cost is larger than the criterion: without it the browser will not fill these from a saved profile, so every visitor retypes their own name and address.

`autocomplete="name"` and `autocomplete="email"`. The order-number and message fields have no standard purpose and should stay as they are.

For comparison, `/login` and `/signup` already set `autoComplete="email"`, so this is the contact form having missed something the account pages did.

## 2. `/contact` renders two `<main>` elements

`apps/web/src/app/contact/page.tsx` opens a `<main>`, and the surrounding layout supplies one too. Two `main` landmarks on one page means a screen-reader user's "jump to main content" has two destinations and neither is the whole content.

One of the two should become a `<div>` — most likely the page's, since the layout's is the one that applies to every route.

## Why neither was fixed in #196

#196 changes the boundary colour of ten fields. Both of these are structural and neither is affected by it. Filed rather than folded in, per the runbook.

issues.title: A failed categories fetch renders as a heading with nothing under it
issues.body:
Found by `ui-review` while rendering PR #300 (a `next` 16.3.0 -> 16.3.1 bump). Pre-existing; the bump changed nothing rendered. ## The code `apps/web/src/components/sidebar-wrapper.tsx`: ```js } catch (error) { console.error("Failed to fetch categories", error); } ``` That is the whole error path. `categories` stays at its initial `[]`, and the drawer renders: ```html

Shop

    ``` A section heading with an empty list under it. No error text, no retry, nothing that distinguishes "we could not load the catalogue" from "there is nothing to shop for". ## How it was seen `/api/categories` returned 500 because the review environment had no database running. That part is environmental — but the *handling* is not, and it would look identical in production for any reason the fetch fails: a deploy where the API is briefly unavailable, a network error on a flaky connection, a 500 from the database. The console line is the only signal, and it goes to a console no visitor opens. ## Why this shape matters here specifically This is the repository's recorded signature defect wearing different clothes. The one #148 keeps naming is a *check* that runs without asserting on what it produced; this is a *UI* that renders without asserting on what it received. Both fail silently and both look fine. #137 was a category page referencing an image that had never existed, and #141 was a seed writing credentials that could never authenticate — each green, each invisible until someone looked. An empty `
      ` under a "Shop" heading is the user-facing member of that family. ## Suggested fix Distinguish the three states the component currently collapses into one: loading, loaded-and-empty, and failed. The failed state needs visible text and ideally a retry; loaded-and-empty needs different wording, if it is even reachable. Worth checking while there: whether `sidebar-wrapper.test.tsx` can cover the failure branch. It currently has one test, `should fetch categories and render sidebar`, which exercises only the success path — so nothing today would notice if the error branch stopped rendering at all. ## Why it was not fixed at the time Found during a dependency-bump review whose diff is two lines of `package.json`.

issues.title: The drawer trigger has no focus indicator, and #306 made it a focus destination
issues.body:
Found by `code-review` during #306. Pre-existing, and already recorded — `apps/web/src/lib/control-classes.ts:26` says so outright:

> the chat launcher is one, sits outside the dialog, and nothing reads its accent. The header's `Open menu` has no focus accent at all, which predates any of this.

So the gap is known. What changed is its consequence.

## Why #306 makes it matter more

Before #306, the trigger was a control you could tab to. After it, the trigger is where focus is **deliberately sent**: closing the drawer by Escape, the Close button, or the backdrop returns focus to it, precisely so the next Tab continues from where the user was instead of restarting at the top of the document.

That return is invisible. A sighted keyboard user dismisses the drawer and focus lands on a control with no focus indicator at all — so the mechanism works and the feedback does not, which is close to the worst of both: the page state is correct and unreadable.

It is also clipped, from a separate cause: `position: static` and `-m-2.5` put the trigger's rect at `[-1, 43]`, so its top pixel is above the viewport at `scrollY=0` and cannot be painted. Any indicator added here is clipped at the top edge until that offset changes.

## Not the same decision as #315, but next to it

#315 is about the drawer's *contents* — its Close button and nav links drawing the UA default `outline: auto 1px` while page controls use `ACTION_BOUNDARY`/`ACTION_FOCUS`. This is about the trigger, which sits in the header, outside the drawer.

They should probably be decided together, because both turn on the axis `control-classes.ts` documents: focus colour is indigo on the page and sky-700 inside the chat widget, chosen in #184 so the panel reads as its own place, with #236 naming the axis as *location*. The trigger is unambiguously page furniture, so indigo and `ACTION_FOCUS` is the likely answer here — which makes this the smaller and less contentious half of the pair.

## Why it was not fixed in #306

`code-review` classified it as outside that change and I agree: the mechanism #306 adds is correct without it, the accent is a design-system decision rather than a bug fix, and taking it would have pre-empted #315's question inside a pull request scoped to the drawer's dialog semantics.

## Worth checking when fixing

Whether the enforcing spec covers it afterwards. `control-classes.ts` describes `action-controls.spec.ts` as asserting agreement "across the eleven page controls it lists", and the trigger is not among them — so adding the class without adding the control to that list leaves the same silence that let this sit unnoticed.
issues.display_title: The drawer trigger has no focus indicator, and #306 made it a focus destination

issues.title: At phone width an open chat panel makes the navigation drawer unreachable
issues.body:
Found by `ui-review` at 390x844 while rendering #306. Pre-existing and living entirely in `chat.tsx`, which #306 does not touch.

## Measured

`chat.tsx` marks everything beside the chat widget `inert` while its sheet is open below `lg`:

```
main inert = true   at 390x844
main inert = false  at 1440x900
```

`Header` renders inside `<main>`, so the menu trigger is inside the inerted subtree. With the chat sheet open at phone width the trigger is neither focusable nor clickable, and Escape closes the chat rather than doing anything with the menu.

So at phone width the site's navigation is unavailable for as long as the chat panel is open.

## Why this is arguably correct, and arguably not

It is the modal contract working as designed. `chat.tsx` is explicit that below `lg` the sheet is modal — `aria-modal`, a focus trap, and `inert` on everything behind — and "the rest of the page is unavailable" is exactly what a modal claims. On that reading there is nothing to fix: dismiss the chat, then open the menu.

What makes it worth recording anyway is that the two surfaces are peers rather than nested. A modal dialog usually covers a task the user is in the middle of; the nav drawer is how they leave. At phone width the chat sheet takes the whole viewport, so a user who opens chat and then wants to navigate has to discover that closing it is the prerequisite, with no affordance saying so.

It is also asymmetric now. Since #306 the drawer is modal too, but it does not inert the page — it cannot, because it renders *inside* `<main>` rather than beside it, so inerting an ancestor would inert the drawer with it. Two modal surfaces on one page, only one of which suppresses the other, is a state worth having deliberately rather than by accident of where each is mounted.

## Options

1. **Leave it and document it.** The modal contract is honest and the workaround is one tap. Cheapest, and the comment in `chat.tsx` around `isModal` is where it would go.
2. **Exempt the menu trigger from the inert set**, so navigation stays reachable. Contradicts `aria-modal` unless the chat stops claiming to be modal at phone width, which is a larger change and would undo #187's reasoning.
3. **Close the chat when the drawer opens**, making them explicitly exclusive layers. Needs a shared owner for "which overlay is up", which neither component currently has.

## Not established

Whether a user can reach the chat launcher while the drawer is open — the reverse direction was not measured. Worth checking before choosing, since if both directions block each other the answer is more likely (3) than (1).
issues.display_title: At phone width an open chat panel makes the navigation drawer unreachable

issues.title: The drawer's controls are the one keyboard surface no focus-ring guard covers
issues.body:
Found by `ui-review` while rendering #306, at 390x844, 768x1024 and 1440x900. Pre-existing — the sidebar has never carried focus classes — but #306 makes it matter more, because the drawer is now a keyboard-primary surface with a focus trap, so a keyboard user spends time in it by design.

## Measured

With the drawer open, every control inside it draws the browser's default indicator:

```
drawer controls (Close, and each nav link)   outline: auto 1px
header controls (Sign In, Sign Up)           outline: solid 2px, indigo
```

The header's come from `ACTION_BOUNDARY` / `ACTION_FOCUS` in `apps/web/src/lib/control-classes.ts`. The drawer's come from nowhere — it imports none of them.

## Why this is worth more than a cosmetic inconsistency

`control-classes.ts` documents an axis that this repository worked out over several issues: focus colour is **indigo on the page and sky-700 inside the chat widget**, because #184 decided the panel should read as its own place, and #236 named the axis as *location* rather than control type. The drawer is a third location, and it was never given an answer — it just inherits the user agent's.

More to the point, **the guards that hold that axis do not cover it**. `control-classes.ts` says `chat-controls.spec.ts` walks the panel's controls in both shapes and `action-controls.spec.ts` asserts agreement across "the eleven page controls it lists". The drawer's controls are in neither list, so nothing would notice if they drifted further — and nothing noticed that they never arrived.

That is the same gap shape as #154 (the agent-name guard only covering names below one heading): a guard that reads a list, and a surface that is not on it.

## Decide the answer before writing it

This needs a decision rather than a patch, which is why it is filed rather than fixed inside #306:

- **Indigo, like the rest of the page.** The drawer is site navigation, not its own place in the way the chat panel is. Simplest, and consistent with #236's location axis if the drawer counts as "the page".
- **Its own accent**, if the drawer is judged a distinct location the way the chat widget is. Costs a third colour and needs a reason as good as #184's.

Whichever, the enforcing spec should gain the drawer's controls, or this recurs silently.

## Not established

Whether the UA default `auto 1px` currently passes WCAG 2.4.11/1.4.11 against the drawer's white panel. `ui-review` reported axe clean with the drawer open at all three viewports, and axe does not evaluate focus-indicator contrast, so "no violations" is not evidence either way here. Worth measuring before deciding this is purely cosmetic.
issues.display_title: The drawer's controls are the one keyboard surface no focus-ring guard covers

issues.title: seed_gcp_all.py reinstalls on every run and pip-installs vertexai outside the constraints policy
issues.body:
Found by `code-review` during #294, while it was checking which files in the repository reach `vertexai`. Pre-existing and unrelated to that bump.

Two defects in `install_requirements()` in `infrastructure/scripts/seed_gcp_all.py`, lines 62-80.

## 1. The "already installed" check can never pass

```python
for package in requirements:
    try:
        importlib.import_module(package.replace('-', '_'))
        logger.debug(f"Package {package} already installed")
    except ImportError:
        logger.info(f"Installing {package}...")
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", package], ...)
```

`package.replace('-', '_')` turns `google-cloud-discoveryengine` into `google_cloud_discoveryengine`, which is not an importable module name. The real ones are `google.cloud.aiplatform` and `google.cloud.discoveryengine_v1`. Measured against a venv that has both packages installed:

```
google_cloud_aiplatform      -> ImportError: No module named 'google_cloud_aiplatform'
google_cloud_discoveryengine -> ImportError: No module named 'google_cloud_discoveryengine'
```

So the `except ImportError` branch is taken every time and the `logger.debug("already installed")` branch is unreachable. The script shells out to `pip install` on every invocation regardless of state.

Distribution names and import names are simply different namespaces, and `replace('-', '_')` is the mapping people reach for when they assume otherwise. It happens to work for flat packages, which is why it survives.

## 2. It installs `vertexai`, unpinned, outside the constraints policy

The list is:

```python
requirements = [
    "google-cloud-discoveryengine",
    "google-cloud-aiplatform",
    "vertexai"
]
```

and the install is a bare `pip install <package>` with **no `-c constraints.txt`**.

Two problems, and the second is the sharp one:

- It bypasses the dependency policy entirely. `services/chat/AGENTS.md` says "dependency versions belong in `constraints.txt`", and `check_dependency_policy.py` exists to hold that. A `pip install` with no constraint file can move any of these to any version.
- **`vertexai` is the package this repository deliberately excludes.** `services/chat/src/api/requirements-core.txt` says so explicitly, in a comment written for exactly this reason:

  > The standalone `vertexai` package is deliberately absent: it pins google-cloud-aiplatform to an exact version, which blocks every aiplatform bump. google-cloud-aiplatform ships the `vertexai` module itself.

  So running this script can pull `google-cloud-aiplatform` off its pin as a side effect — the precise outcome that comment exists to prevent, undone by a script in another directory.

Combined with (1), that install runs on every invocation rather than once.

## Fix

The presence check either wants a real distribution lookup (`importlib.metadata.version(package)`) or should be deleted — `pip install` is already idempotent, so the check is buying very little. Drop `vertexai` from the list, since `google-cloud-aiplatform` provides the module. If the install stays, it needs `-c services/chat/constraints.txt` like every other install path in this repository.

## Not established

Whether this script is still used, and against which environment. It lives under `infrastructure/scripts/` rather than in the chat service, and nothing in the documented command surface (`make help`, the npm scripts) invokes it. If it is dead, deleting it is a better fix than repairing it — and #151 is the precedent, where a stale script writing into `public/images` was resolved by settling whether it was still anyone's tool.
issues.display_title: seed_gcp_all.py reinstalls on every run and pip-installs vertexai outside the constraints policy

issues.title: vertexai.generative_models is past its announced removal date, and five chat files import it
issues.body:
Found while verifying #294 (`google-cloud-aiplatform` 1.163.0 -> 1.164.0). Not caused by that bump — the same condition holds at 1.163.0 — but the bump is what put a spotlight on it, and the timing makes it worth acting on rather than filing and forgetting.

## Measured

From the installed package's own `METADATA`, identical in 1.163.0 and 1.164.0:

> The following Generative AI modules in the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform SDK are deprecated as of June 24, 2025 and will be removed on **June 24, 2026**

Today is **2026-08-17**. That removal date passed 54 days ago and the modules are still shipping — verified by importing them under `-W error::DeprecationWarning` on 1.164.0, which raises nothing.

So the deprecation window has expired, the removal has not happened yet, and the changelog carries no further notice. The next release that does remove it is under no obligation to announce it again.

## What breaks when it lands

Five files import the affected surface directly:

```
services/chat/src/api/contoso_chat/chat_request.py
services/chat/src/api/evaluators/custom_evals/coherence.py
services/chat/src/api/evaluators/custom_evals/fluency.py
services/chat/src/api/evaluators/custom_evals/groundedness.py
services/chat/src/api/evaluators/custom_evals/relevance.py
```

`chat_request.py` is the live GCP chat path, not just evaluation tooling.

## Why the usual "CI will catch it" does not reassure here

It will catch the *import*, because `tests/unit/test_evaluators.py` performs a real `import vertexai` and a real `vertexai.init(...)` against the installed package. So a removal produces a red dependabot PR rather than a silent break. That much is fine.

What CI cannot catch is anything subtler, and this is the part worth recording: **nothing in this repository ever makes a real, credentialed `generate_content` call at any version.**

- `tests/unit/test_chat_request.py::test_generate_llm_response_gcp_provider` replaces `sys.modules["vertexai"]` and `sys.modules["vertexai.generative_models"]` with fakes, so it never touches the installed package.
- `tests/unit/test_evaluators.py` does import for real and does call `vertexai.init` for real, but mocks `GenerativeModel` before `generate_content`.
- `make e2e-smoke` never reaches vertexai at all. It raises earlier, at `services/chat/src/api/search_service.py:95` — `PROJECT_ID, REGION, and DISCOVERY_ENGINE_DATASTORE_ID must be set` — before `generate_llm_response` is called. Setting `E2E_REQUIRE_REAL_CHAT=1` does not help; it fails for missing datastore config instead.

That is a standing coverage gap rather than something this bump introduced, but it bounds what any green run can tell you about this dependency: it proves the import surface resolves, and nothing about behaviour.

## Options

1. **Migrate to the Google Gen AI SDK** (`google-genai`), which is what the deprecation notice directs users to. Real work across five files, and it changes the live chat path, so it wants its own slice and its own testing story.
2. **Pin `google-cloud-aiplatform` and stop taking bumps** until the migration is done, so removal cannot arrive unannounced. It is already pinned exactly, so this means a dependabot ignore rule rather than a code change — and it trades a sudden break for a knowingly stale dependency.
3. **Leave it and rely on CI's import-level catch**, having recorded here what the failure will look like and which five files it lands in.

Option 1 is the only one that ends it. Whether it is worth doing now depends on how much the GCP provider path is actually used, which is not established here — `LLM_PROVIDER=local` is the documented local default, and the smoke has never exercised the GCP path for real.

## Not established

- Whether `google-genai` covers everything the four evaluators and `chat_request.py` need, or whether the migration changes behaviour as well as imports.
- Whether the removal is genuinely imminent or whether the date has quietly slipped. Two months past with no removal suggests slippage, but that is an inference from one observation and this repository has a written history of those being wrong.
issues.display_title: vertexai.generative_models is past its announced removal date, and five chat files import it

issues.title: google-cloud-storage is an unpinned transitive dep that aiplatform has announced it will drop
issues.body:
Found while verifying #294 (`google-cloud-aiplatform` 1.163.0 -> 1.164.0). Pre-existing — the warning fires at 1.163.0 too — and unrelated to that bump, which is why it is filed rather than fixed there.

## Measured

Importing the chat service's own dependency prints:

```
.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/google/cloud/aiplatform/models.py:52: FutureWarning:
Support for google-cloud-storage < 3.0.0 will be removed in a future version of
google-cloud-aiplatform. Please upgrade to google-cloud-storage >= 3.0.0.
```

What is actually installed, and where it comes from:

```
$ pip show google-cloud-storage
Version: 2.19.0
Required-by: google-cloud-aiplatform

$ grep google-cloud services/chat/constraints.txt
google-cloud-aiplatform==1.164.0
google-cloud-discoveryengine==0.20.2
```

So `google-cloud-storage` is **transitive and unpinned**. It appears in no requirements file and no constraint. Its version is whatever pip resolves under `google-cloud-aiplatform`'s own bounds, which today land on 2.19.0 — the range the warning is announcing the end of.

## Why this is worth a decision rather than a shrug

Two things make it more than warning noise.

**It contradicts the stated dependency policy.** `services/chat/AGENTS.md` says "dependency versions belong in `constraints.txt`", and `services/chat/scripts/check_dependency_policy.py` enforces exactly that correspondence — its docstring is "Versions live in exactly one place." That guard covers packages named in a requirements manifest. A transitive dependency named in none is invisible to it, which is the same shape as #118 (`check_dependency_policy.py` cannot catch an import with no manifest entry) seen from the other end: #118 is an import with no entry, this is a version with no entry.

**The break arrives inside somebody else's PR.** When `aiplatform` does drop support, the failure surfaces as a dependabot bump of `aiplatform` — with the actual cause being a package that appears nowhere in this repository. That is a bad debugging start, and it is avoidable now while the warning still says "will be".

## Options

1. **Pin `google-cloud-storage` in `constraints.txt` at 2.19.0.** Makes the current state explicit and visible to dependabot, which would then propose the 3.x move as its own reviewable PR. Costs an entry for a package nothing imports directly, which `check_dependency_policy.py` may reject as an inert pin — worth checking, since it validates in both directions.
2. **Move to `google-cloud-storage >= 3.0.0` now**, ahead of the deadline. Whether aiplatform 1.164.0 permits 3.x is not established here and needs checking first.
3. **Leave it and let the eventual aiplatform bump force the issue**, having recorded here what the failure will look like so whoever meets it does not start from zero.

## Not established

- Whether `google-cloud-aiplatform` 1.164.0 already accepts `google-cloud-storage >= 3.0.0`, which decides whether option 2 is available today or is blocked on a further aiplatform bump.
- Whether anything in the chat service actually reaches the `gcs_utils` code path that the warning guards, or whether this is a warning about a capability this service never uses. That changes the urgency substantially and is the first thing worth checking.
issues.display_title: google-cloud-storage is an unpinned transitive dep that aiplatform has announced it will drop

issues.title: evaluate.py passes to_markdown's mode positionally, which pandas 4.0 removes
issues.body:
Found while verifying #294 (a `google-cloud-aiplatform` bump). Pre-existing and unrelated to that PR — it is one of the two warnings every chat test run has been printing.

## Measured

`services/chat/src/api/evaluate.py:110`:

```python
mean_df.to_markdown('eval_results.md', 'a')
```

The second positional argument is `mode`. pandas already warns on it, on every run of `make -C services/chat ci`:

```
tests/unit/test_evaluate.py::test_create_summary_writes_markdown
  services/chat/src/api/evaluate.py:110: Pandas4Warning: Starting with pandas
  version 4.0 all arguments of to_markdown except for the argument 'buf' will
  be keyword-only.
```

`pandas` is pinned at `3.0.5` in `services/chat/constraints.txt`, so nothing breaks today. It breaks the first time dependabot proposes pandas 4.x.

Line 107 two lines above is fine — `df.to_markdown('eval_results.md')` passes only `buf`.

## Fix

```python
mean_df.to_markdown('eval_results.md', mode='a')
```

## Why file it rather than leave it for the bump to find

It will be found either way: `test_create_summary_writes_markdown` covers this path, so a pandas 4 bump fails CI rather than shipping broken. But it fails as a *dependabot PR that looks like it broke something*, which is the most confusing shape for the person triaging it — the diff will be one version line and the failure will be in unrelated application code.

Fixing it now costs one keyword and turns that future PR back into a routine bump. It also removes one of exactly two warnings from the chat test output, and a suite with no warnings is one where a new warning is visible.

The other warning is filed separately — it is a transitive-dependency question rather than a line of our code.
